1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
     9	975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
    10	follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
    11	`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
    12	the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
    13	`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
    14	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
    15	from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
    16	for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    17	replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
    18	`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
    19	nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
    20	scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
    21	corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
    22	matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
    23	edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
    24	Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
    25	a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
    26	`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
    27	cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
    28	every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
    29	same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
    30	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    31	(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
    32	(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
    33	moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
    34	two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
    35	(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    36	
    37	## Scope
    38	
    39	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    40	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    41	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
    42	  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (whole-result modules);
    43	  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
    44	- The rows cover every public theorem (1747) and 361 definitions whose
    45	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 81
    46	  public definitions have no rows of their own: 77 (for example `kappa`,
    47	  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,
    48	  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`, `SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure` and
    49	  `TerminalWick.chainMassReal`) only name quantities or measures used in
    50	  those statements, and four are the instances that make
    51	  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the
    52	  Lean source or in `Audit/`.
    53	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    54	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    55	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    56	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    57	- The sixty-six `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    58	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and time-fractional
    59	  foundation of `ClockCopy`, `GaussianTest` is the Gaussian-test foundation
    60	  of `MaskedSpectralGrowth`, and `VariationalFloor` and `SeriesType` are
    61	  foundations added in wave L6, `H1Density` one added in wave L7 and
    62	  `FiniteWick` (the finite Wick formula) one added in wave L8;
    63	  `SpatialFourierBound`, added in wave L6 as a foundation, formalizes
    64	  `L:spatial-fourier-bound`, which the manuscript states since revision
    65	  `a284420`) model `H:homog` and formalize the conclusions of forty-eight
    66	  labelled results, to the scopes specified below (some with a narrower
    67	  conclusion, stated per result). Forty-three need no supplied input:
    68	  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own hypotheses.
    69	  `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are proved under weaker
    70	  hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no `delta < 1`) and also
    71	  stated exactly as the manuscript does by the wrappers
    72	  `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the Rayleigh
    73	  lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is not
    74	  formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
    75	  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under the
    76	  full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance` models
    77	  clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,
    78	  temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges).
    79	  `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` and `L:temporal-equilibrium` are stated with
    80	  the manuscript's own hypotheses (`gamma_beta_paper`,
    81	  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,
    82	  `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
    83	  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`, is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses
    84	  (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability space) on top
    85	  of a finite Gaussian integration-by-parts foundation (`GaussianIBP`).
    86	  `L:variational-control-dilation` is stated with the section's hypotheses
    87	  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
    88	  `variational_control_dilation_paper`, for the cost in its integral form

   384	supported function (Mathlib's `MemLp.exists_hasCompactSupport_eLpNorm_sub_le`). -/
   385	private theorem exists_compact_approx (f : Lp ℝ 2 (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))))
   386	    {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) :
   387	    ∃ (g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ) (hg : MemLp g 2 volume),
   388	      HasCompactSupport g ∧ ‖f - hg.toLp g‖ ≤ η := by
   389	  obtain ⟨g, hgc, hle, -, hg⟩ := (Lp.memLp f).exists_hasCompactSupport_eLpNorm_sub_le
   390	    ENNReal.ofNat_ne_top (ENNReal.ofReal_pos.mpr hη).ne'
   391	  refine ⟨g, hg, hgc, ?_⟩
   392	  have hf : f = (Lp.memLp f).toLp f := (Lp.toLp_coeFn f (Lp.memLp f)).symm
   393	  rw [hf, ← MemLp.toLp_sub, Lp.norm_toLp]
   394	  exact ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal hη.le hle
   395	
   396	/-- Auxiliary: a compactly supported function vanishes outside a ball. -/
   397	private theorem exists_bound_of_hasCompactSupport {g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ}
   398	    (hg : HasCompactSupport g) : ∃ R : ℝ, ∀ x, ‖x‖ > R → g x = 0 := by
   399	  obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := isBounded_iff_forall_norm_le.mp hg.isCompact.isBounded
   400	  refine ⟨R, fun x hx => ?_⟩
   401	  by_contra h
   402	  exact absurd (hR x (subset_tsupport g h)) (not_le.mpr hx)
   403	
   404	/-- Auxiliary: translated pairings of compactly supported `L²` functions vanish for
   405	`|y|` large. -/
   406	private theorem inner_transL2_eventually_zero {f g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ}
   407	    (hf : MemLp f 2 volume) (hg : MemLp g 2 volume) (hfc : HasCompactSupport f)
   408	    (hgc : HasCompactSupport g) :
   409	    ∀ᶠ y in Filter.cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
   410	      inner ℝ (transL2 d y (hf.toLp f)) (hg.toLp g) = 0 := by
   411	  obtain ⟨R₁, hR₁⟩ := exists_bound_of_hasCompactSupport hfc
   412	  obtain ⟨R₂, hR₂⟩ := exists_bound_of_hasCompactSupport hgc
   413	  filter_upwards [tendsto_norm_cocompact_atTop.eventually (Filter.eventually_gt_atTop (R₁ + R₂))]
   414	    with y hy
   415	  rw [L2.inner_def]
   416	  refine integral_eq_zero_of_ae ?_
   417	  have h1 : (transL2 d y (hf.toLp f) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ) =ᵐ[volume]
   418	      fun x => f (x - y) := by
   419	    have := Lp.coeFn_compMeasurePreserving (hf.toLp f) (measurePreserving_sub_right volume y)
   420	    refine this.trans ?_
   421	    exact (measurePreserving_sub_right volume y).quasiMeasurePreserving.ae_eq_comp
   422	      (MemLp.coeFn_toLp hf)
   423	  filter_upwards [h1, MemLp.coeFn_toLp hg] with x hx1 hx2
   424	  rw [hx1, hx2]
   425	  by_cases hx : ‖x‖ > R₂
   426	  · simp [hR₂ x hx]
   427	  · have : ‖x - y‖ > R₁ := by
   428	      have := norm_sub_norm_le y x
   429	      rw [norm_sub_rev] at this
   430	      linarith [not_lt.mp hx]
   431	    simp [hR₁ _ this]
   432	
   433	/-- Auxiliary: the translations of `L²(ℝ^d)` are weakly null as `|y| → ∞`, by
   434	density of continuous compactly supported functions. -/
   435	private theorem transL2_weak (z w : Lp ℝ 2 (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))) :
   436	    Filter.Tendsto (fun y => inner ℝ (transL2 d y z) w)
   437	      (Filter.cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) (nhds 0) := by
   438	  have hnorm : ∀ y u, ‖transL2 d y u‖ = ‖u‖ := fun y u =>
   439	    Lp.norm_compMeasurePreserving u (measurePreserving_sub_right volume y)
   440	  -- Step 1: `w` compactly supported, `z` arbitrary.
   441	  have step1 : ∀ (g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ) (hg : MemLp g 2 volume),
   442	      HasCompactSupport g → ∀ z : Lp ℝ 2 (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))),
   443	      Filter.Tendsto (fun y => inner ℝ (transL2 d y z) (hg.toLp g))
   444	        (Filter.cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) (nhds 0) := by
   445	    intro g hg hgc z
   446	    refine tendsto_zero_of_forall_approx fun ε hε => ?_
   447	    obtain ⟨f, hf, hfc, hzf⟩ := exists_compact_approx z
   448	      (η := ε / (‖hg.toLp g‖ + 1)) (by positivity)
   449	    refine ⟨fun y => inner ℝ (transL2 d y (hf.toLp f)) (hg.toLp g),
   450	      tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_eq (inner_transL2_eventually_zero hf hg hfc hgc),
   451	      fun y => ?_⟩
   452	    rw [← inner_sub_left, ← map_sub]
   453	    refine (abs_real_inner_le_norm _ _).trans ?_
   454	    rw [hnorm]
   455	    calc ‖z - hf.toLp f‖ * ‖hg.toLp g‖ ≤ ε / (‖hg.toLp g‖ + 1) * (‖hg.toLp g‖ + 1) := by
   456	          gcongr; linarith
   457	      _ = ε := by field_simp
   458	  -- Step 2: arbitrary `w`.
   459	  refine tendsto_zero_of_forall_approx fun ε hε => ?_
   460	  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgc, hwg⟩ := exists_compact_approx w
   461	    (η := ε / (‖z‖ + 1)) (by positivity)
   462	  refine ⟨fun y => inner ℝ (transL2 d y z) (hg.toLp g), step1 g hg hgc z, fun y => ?_⟩
   463	  rw [← inner_sub_right]
   464	  refine (abs_real_inner_le_norm _ _).trans ?_
   465	  rw [hnorm]
   466	  calc ‖z‖ * ‖w - hg.toLp g‖ ≤ (‖z‖ + 1) * (ε / (‖z‖ + 1)) := by
   467	        gcongr; linarith [norm_nonneg z]
   468	    _ = ε := by field_simp
   469	
   470	/-- **The supplied structure `SymplecticFree.FreeWaveData d E` is not vacuous**: for
   471	every `d` it has an instance on the real Hilbert space `E = L²(ℝ^d)` (Lebesgue measure),
   472	which is not the zero space.  The witness: `S_E(h) = I` for all `h`, `𝓡 = I`, and
   473	`τ_y f = f(· - y)` the genuine spatial translations; they are isometric, commute with
   474	`S_E`, and `⟨τ_y z, w⟩ → 0` as `|y| → ∞` is proved for all `z, w ∈ L²(ℝ^d)` (pairings of
   475	compactly supported functions vanish for large `|y|`; general `z, w` by density of
   476	continuous compactly supported functions, `transL2_weak`).
   477	
   478	What this shows: the fields of `FreeWaveData` (the structure that stands for the
   479	objects of `notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex` lines 103-122 at revision a284420,
   480	used by `L:symplectic-free`, lines 30-133) are jointly satisfiable on a nonzero space
   481	with translations that are genuinely weakly null, so the theorems taking a
   482	`FreeWaveData` (for example `SymplecticFree.compact_young_baseline`) do not hold
   483	vacuously.  What it does not show: the witness's `S_E` is the trivial group, not the
   484	free wave group on `H^{1/2} × H^{-1/2}`, and `𝓡` is not the velocity reversal; the
   485	concrete instance of the TeX (free wave group, Bessel-norm space, Riemann-Lebesgue
   486	argument of lines 105-110) is not constructed. -/
   487	theorem freeWaveData_nonempty (d : ℕ) :
   488	    Nonempty (SymplecticFree.FreeWaveData d
   489	      (Lp ℝ 2 (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))))) :=
   490	  ⟨{ S := fun _ => 1
   491	     S_zero := rfl
   492	     S_add := fun _ _ => (mul_one _).symm
   493	     R := 1
   494	     R_norm := fun _ => rfl
   495	     S_neg := fun _ => by simp
   496	     τ := transL2 d
   497	     τ_norm := fun y u => Lp.norm_compMeasurePreserving u (measurePreserving_sub_right volume y)
   498	     τ_comm := fun _ _ => by simp
   499	     τ_weak := fun z w => transL2_weak z w }⟩
   500

  1410	   98| \begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
  1411	   99|   \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
  1412	  100|   On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
  1413	  101|   $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
  1414	  102|   h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
  1415	  103|   positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
  1416	  104|   \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
  1417	  105|     \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
  1418	  106|     =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
  1419	  107|     \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
  1420	  108|   \end{equation}
  1421	  109|   It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
  1422	  110|   positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
  1423	  111| \end{proposition}
  1424	  112| 
  1425	  113| \begin{proof}
  1426	  114|   The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
  1427	  115|   multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
  1428	  116|   -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
  1429	  117|   densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
  1430	  118|   equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
  1431	  119|   \[
  1432	  120|     H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
  1433	  121|   \]
  1434	  122|   The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
  1435	  123|   1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
  1436	  124|   \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
  1437	  125|   \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
  1438	  126|   $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
  1439	  127| 
  1440	  128|   Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
  1441	  129|   Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
  1442	  130|   \[
  1443	  131|     \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
  1444	  132|     \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
  1445	  133|     \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
  1446	  134|   \]
  1447	  135|   Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
  1448	  136|   half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
  1449	  137|   equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
  1450	  138|   both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
  1451	  139| 
  1452	  140|   The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
  1453	  141|   reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
  1454	  142|   vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
  1455	  143|   because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
  1456	  144|   $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
  1457	  145|   q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
  1458	  146|   real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The

    93	  \label{P:raw-occupation-energy}

   106	    &=\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}}}{2-\alpha}\right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}
   107	    \left(\frac{2\zeta}{\alpha}\right)^{\alpha/2}.

   111	  $\zeta^{-\alpha/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_1^{\mathcal{O}}$.

   114	\begin{proof}
   115	  A unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy: a zero weak gradient makes
   116	  it constant, and an $L^2$ constant on $\R^d$ is zero. Hence, $0 < T(g) <
   117	  \infty$. Spatial covariance Cauchy--Schwarz gives $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   118	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}b_s^{\alpha/4}b_t^{\alpha/4}$. Schur with row bound $K_0$, then
   119	  concavity, proves
   120	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-occupation-bound}
   121	    0\le A(g)\le K_0R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}.
   122	  \end{equation}

   124	  $\mathcal{O}$ and has positive $A$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   125	  This proves positivity and finiteness of $C_{\rm occ}$.
   126	
   127	  The map $(U_\ell g)_s(x) = \ell^{d/2}g_s(\ell x)$ is an $H^1$ isomorphism
   128	  preserving unit mass and strong measurability. It has inverse $U_{1/\ell}$ and
   129	  is a bijection on $\mathcal{O}$. The physical Radon change of variables gives
   130	  \[
   131	    A(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A(g),\qquad
   132	    T(U_\ell g)=\ell^2T(g).

   135	  $\ell^{-d}$, and the pushforward of $\Gamma$ contributes $\ell^{\alpha-d}$.

   137	  $g,\ell$ leaves the class unchanged. For fixed $A,T > 0$, the derivative of
   138	  $A\ell^\alpha-\zeta T\ell^2$ has the sign of $\alpha A-2\zeta
   139	  T\ell^{2-\alpha}$. Its global maximum occurs at $\ell = (\alpha A/(2\zeta
   140	  T))^{1/(2-\alpha)}$ and equals $D_\zeta[A/T^{\alpha/2}]^{2/(2-\alpha)}$. For

   143	  ratios approaching its positive supremum give the other by continuity of the
   144	  positive power. Algebra gives~\eqref{E:raw-occupation-ratio} and the penalty
   145	  scaling. No optimizer or minimax interchange is assumed. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-occupation-energy}.

   162	  density therefore supplies a countable real family. Discard zero and normalize
   163	  each member in $L^2$ to obtain $f_j$ dense in the $L^2$-unit $H^1$ class.

    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define

   156	  Consequently,
   157	  \[
   158	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\le8b\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(2\sqrt b)
   159	    =2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2}.
   160	  \]
   161	  Nonnegativity follows from the spectral identity. If $\Gamma=0$, then
   162	  $\mu=0$ and both sides of~\eqref{E:spatial-fourier-bound} vanish. This proves
   163	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound}.
   164	\end{proof}
   165	
   166	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
   167	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}
   168	  For real unit $g \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ put $R(g) =
   169	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   170	  a positive finite real number, and
   171	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   172	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
   173	    k\left[
   174	    \frac{R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}}{8M_aq^{q/2}}
   175	    \right]^{1/k}.
   176	  \end{equation}
   177	\end{proposition}
   178	
   179	\begin{proof}
   180	  The gradient energy $b(g)$ is positive: a nonzero $L^2$ function with zero
   181	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   182	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   183	  autocorrelation argument in the proof of
   184	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} gives
   185	  $0 < A:=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)<\infty$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound} gives
   186	  $R(g)\le2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha$ for every such profile. A normalized compact
   187	  bump supplies a positive ratio. Thus, $0<R_0<\infty$, independently of the
   188	  finiteness of $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$. It remains to prove the score inequality.
   189	  With $U_\ell g(x)=\ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the physical changes of variables give
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   191	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   192	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   193	  \end{equation}
   194	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   195	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   196	
   197	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   198	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   199	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   200	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   201	  \[
   202	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   203	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   204	  \]
   205	  The radicand is $L^2$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} consequently
   206	  gives
   207	  \[
   208	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   209	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   210	  \]
   211	  Its maximum occurs at $L^k = 1/(qC)$ and is $(k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}$. Since $1+u =
   212	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,
   213	  proving~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score}. This argument retains the finite
   214	  real value $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ fixed at the start of the section; only the
   215	  proof of $R_0<\infty$ is independent of that input. This proves
   216	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.
   217	\end{proof}
   218	
   219	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]
   220	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   221	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   222	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   223	  \begin{align}
   224	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   225	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   226	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   227	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   228	  \end{align}
   229	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   230	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   232	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   233	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   234	  \end{equation}
   235	  The ratio supremum $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over all real unit $H^1$ profiles equals
   236	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.
   237	\end{proposition}
   238	
   239	\begin{proof}
   240	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   241	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   242	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   243	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   244	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   245	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   246	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   247	  convention gives
   248	  \[
   249	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   250	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   251	  \]
   252	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   253	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   254	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   255	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   256	  \[
   257	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   258	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   259	  \]
   260	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   261	
   262	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   263	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   264	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   265	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   266	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   267	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   268	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   269	
   270	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   271	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   272	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   273	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   274	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   275	  continuity.
   276	
   277	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   278	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   279	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   280	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   281	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   282	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   283	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   284	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   285	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   286	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   287	
   288	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   289	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   290	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   291	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   292	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   293	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   294	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   295	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   296	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   297	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   298	\end{proof}
   299	
   300	\begin{proposition}[The spatial energy and static lower variational expression]
   301	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}
   302	  Over all real unit $H^1$ profiles define the energy
   303	  \[
   304	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   305	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}
   306	    \left(A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)-\frac{b(g)}2\right).
   307	  \]
   308	  Then
   309	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-energy-map}
   310	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   311	    =\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   312	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{2/(2-\alpha)}
   313	    \in(0,\infty).
   314	  \end{equation}
   315	  In particular,
   316	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   317	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}),
   318	    \qquad
   319	    F_0(z)=k\left[
   320	    \frac{(2z/(2-\alpha))^{(2-\alpha)/2}}{8q^{q/2}}
   321	    \right]^{1/k},\quad z>0.
   322	  \end{equation}
   323	  The subscript in $F_0$ labels this scalar map; the covariance retains its
   324	  original temporal exponent $a$.
   325	\end{proposition}
   326	
   327	\begin{proof}
   328	  Physical change of variables, or smooth approximation and
   329	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, extends \eqref{E:spatial-dilation} to
   330	  real $H^1$ profiles. For fixed unit $g$, with $A,b > 0$, the maximum of
   331	  $\ell^\alpha A-\ell^2b/2$ occurs at $\ell^{2-\alpha} = \alpha A/b$ and equals
   332	  \[
   333	    \frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   334	    R(g)^{2/(2-\alpha)}.
   335	  \]
   336	  Dilation preserves the whole unit class and includes $\ell = 1$. Taking both
   337	  numerical suprema, then profiles with ratio tending to $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$,
   338	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. No optimizer is assumed. Smooth ratios
   339	  also approach $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   340	  Pass them through~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score} and substitute
   341	  \[
   342	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}\alpha^{\alpha/2}
   343	    =\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}}{2-\alpha}
   344	    \right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}.
   345	  \]
   346	  This gives~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}. This proves
   347	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-energy-map}.
   348	\end{proof}

     3	/-
     4	Copyright 2026 Le Chen. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
     5	
     6	Hypothesis `H:homog` of the manuscript (main TeX file, Section `S:model`),
     7	stated in full as a Lean predicate, and the two results that the manuscript
     8	states under it, `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters`, restated with this
     9	hypothesis. Their proofs use only the numerical part of `H:homog`
    10	(`KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo`, `DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty`); the
    11	covariance part is carried as hypotheses exactly as the manuscript states
    12	them, so these wrappers have the manuscript's own hypotheses.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	public import Mathlib
    16	public import StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.KappaRange
    17	public import StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.DriverParameters
    18	
    19	@[expose] public section
    20	
    21	noncomputable section
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	open MeasureTheory
    26	open scoped Pointwise
    27	
    28	namespace StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.HomogHypothesis
    29	
    30	/-- Euclidean space `ℝ^d`. -/
    31	abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
    32	
    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩
    88	
    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range
    96	
    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)
   104	
   105	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.HomogHypothesis

    11	orthogonality, nor coefficient extraction in `r`, nor scaling of the field.  It
    12	expands `E|u(r)|² = Σ_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`; all mixed moments
    13	`E[Y_m Y_n]` are nonnegative (`L:terminal-wick`, TeX lines 3600-3645, for a
    14	field with nonnegative covariance), and `r > 0`, so the double sum dominates its
    15	diagonal term `r^{2n} E|Y_n|²`.

    17	Supplied input (the only one), from `L:terminal-wick`: the structure
    18	`TerminalWickInput`, i.e. for the given `r`, absolute `L²` convergence of
    19	`Σ r^n Y_n` and nonnegativity of every mixed moment `E[Y_m Y_n]`.  These are
    20	exactly the two facts the TeX proof cites from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3730-3731:

225	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   226	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   227	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   228	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the

  3714	    \text{ in }L^2\text{ for each fixed }n.

  3717	  $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1) \to u$ in $L^2$, and

  3720	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad
  3721	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\right\|_2,
  3722	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}X_n\right\|_2
  3723	    \le\frac{B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}.

  3726	  B_1$.

  3733	  so $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2 \le B_r$. Taking the fixed-order $L^2$
  3734	  limit proves the same bound for $X_n$. The geometric series and the triangle
  3735	  inequality give all estimates in~\eqref{E:uniform-series-tail}, including

   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}
   287	  Write $k = 3-\alpha > 0$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $m = q/k > 1$. Fix one
   288	  $\Psi_0$ from the nonempty class and put $I_0 = I_{\Psi_0} > 0$, $v_0 =
   289	  v_{\Psi_0} > 0$. Positivity of the latter is
   290	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}. For $r_0 = (I_0/v_0)^{1/k} > 0$, which need
   291	  not be less than one, the exact real-power identity gives
   292	  \[
   293	    I_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}-v_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}/2
   294	    =r_0I_0-r_0^qv_0/2=r_0I_0/2>0.
   295	  \]
   296	  This positive value is obtained from a smooth nonnegative control.
   297	
   298	  For $c > 0$ put $r_c = c^{1/k}$ and $K_c = c^m > 0$.
   299	  Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation} and the exact scalar powers give,
   300	  for every $\Psi$,
   301	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-set-scaling}
   302	    cI_{D_{r_c}\Psi}-v_{D_{r_c}\Psi}/2
   303	    =K_c(I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2).
   304	  \end{equation}
   305	  Since $D_{r_c}$ is a bijection of the entire class, the whole set of
   306	  variational values with coefficient $c$ is $K_c$ times the whole
   307	  coefficient-one set of variational values.
   308	
   309	  We prove boundedness before taking finite-real suprema. The independent
   310	  Theorem~\ref{T:full-upper}, for the \emph{same canonical solution}, gives
   311	  \[
   312	    \E|u(T,0)|^2\le e(T+2)^d e^{C_{\mathrm{up}}T^\kappa},
   313	    \qquad T\ge1,\quad C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty.
   314	  \]
   315	  Its prefactor is negligible: choose $\epsilon = \kappa/2 > 0$, use $\log T \le
   316	  (T^\epsilon-1)/\epsilon$ and $\log(T+2) \le \log T+\log3$ for $T \ge 1$, and
   317	  divide by $T^\kappa$. Thus, the original point limsup is at most
   318	  $C_{\mathrm{up}}$. One fixed test/mask lower bound gives a finite lower bound
   319	  for $Q_2$, so $Q_2$ is finite. By~\eqref{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}
   320	  every coefficient-two variational expression is at most this same $Q_2 \le
   321	  C_{\mathrm{up}}$, uniformly in $\Psi$.
   322	  Equation~\eqref{E:variational-score-set-scaling} at $c = 2$ consequently
   323	  bounds all coefficient-one variational values by $C_{\mathrm{up}}/K_2$. The
   324	  nonempty set has a finite real supremum $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} > 0$ by the
   325	  positive test above.
   326	
   327	  For general $c$, set equality and $K_c > 0$ show that $K_cS_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   328	  is the supremum: it is an upper bound, and every smaller number is exceeded by
   329	  $K_c$ times a coefficient-one variational expression within the corresponding
   330	  positive distance of its supremum. This proves finiteness, positivity and the
   331	  first identity in~\eqref{E:variational-score-homogeneity}. Taking the
   332	  numerical supremum of the coefficient-two lower bounds proves the second.
   333	  Although $2^m > 2$, the resulting $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}} > 2S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   334	  is only a comparison of auxiliary variational values. It is not a Jensen
   335	  improvement without a first-moment identification. This proves
   336	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
   337	\end{proof}
    30	\begin{lemma}[Free wave form and compact Young baseline]
    31	  \label{L:symplectic-free}
    32	  There is a bounded isometric skew-adjoint $J_E$ on $E$, with $J_E^2 = -I$,
    33	  such that
    34	  \[
    35	    \omega(z,w)=\langle z,J_Ew\rangle_E
    36	    =\langle u,g\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}}
    37	    -\langle f,v\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}},
    38	    \quad z=(u,v),\quad w=(f,g).
    39	  \]
    40	  The free group preserves $\omega$. For bounded real smooth $b$, the force
    41	  $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$ obeys $\omega(B(b)z,w)+\omega(z,B(b)w) = 0$.
    42	
    43	  Let $1/2 < \theta < 1$ and let $X \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{K}(E))$ start at
    44	  zero, with $U_X$ its left Young evolution. Then
    45	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}
    46	    U_X(t,s)-I\in\mathcal{K}(E),\qquad
    47	    \|S_E(t)U_X(t,s)S_E(-s)\|
    48	    \ge\|S_E(t-s)\|\ge1,\qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
    49	  \end{equation}
    50	  More generally, for finitely many such paths $X_j$ starting at zero on $[0,B]$
    51	  and lengths $0 \le \ell_j \le B$, put $P_j = S_E(\ell_j)U_{X_j}(\ell_j,0)$.
    52	  Then
    53	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}
    54	    P_N\cdots P_0-S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\in\mathcal{K}(E),
    55	    \qquad
    56	    \|P_N\cdots P_0\|
    57	    \ge\left\|S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\right\|\ge1 .
    58	  \end{equation}
    59	  These norm bounds require neither Gaussian nor Hamiltonian operator paths.
    60	\end{lemma}
    61	
    62	\begin{proof}
    63	  The balanced map $C_{\rm bal}(u,v) = (\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v)$ is an
    64	  onto real isometry to $L^2\times L^2$. Define $J_{\rm symp}(q,p) = (p,-q)$ and
    65	  $J_E = C_{\rm bal}^{-1}J_{\rm symp}C_{\rm bal}$. This gives all stated
    66	  operator properties and $J_E(f,g) = (\Lambda^{-1}g,-\Lambda f)$. The two
    67	  displayed dualities follow from the balanced $L^2$ pairing. No $L^2$ pairing
    68	  of a general distributional velocity is taken.
    69	
    70	  In balanced Fourier coordinates, the free matrix is
    71	  \[
    72	    W_t(\xi)=
    73	    \begin{pmatrix}
    74	      \cos(tk)&\langle\xi\rangle\sin(tk)/k\\
    75	      -k\sin(tk)/\langle\xi\rangle&\cos(tk)
    76	    \end{pmatrix},\qquad k=|\xi|.
    77	  \]
    78	  At zero it is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, by
    79	  the continuous sine quotient. Direct matrix multiplication gives
    80	  $W_t^{\mathsf{T}}J_{\rm symp}W_t = J_{\rm symp}$, since its determinant is
    81	  $\cos^2(tk)+\sin^2(tk) = 1$, also at zero. The entries are real, even and
    82	  bounded on finite time horizons. Integrating the identity against real-phase
    83	  Fourier vectors with Hermitian symmetry is legitimate by $L^2$
    84	  Cauchy--Schwarz. It gives $\omega(S_E(t)z,S_E(t)w) = \omega(z,w)$ on all $E$.
    85	  Equivalently one may first use Schwartz phases and then density. No rough
    86	  generator derivative or frequency-zero trace is used.
    87	
    88	  Finally, $\|bu\|_{H^{-1/2}} \le \|bu\|_2 \le \|b\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^{1/2}}$.
    89	  Duality for these $L^2$ functions gives the absolutely integrable cancellation
    90	  $-\int fbu+\int ubf = 0$. This is skewness for $\omega$, not for the $E$
    91	  Hilbert inner product. The Young construction of
    92	  Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear} applies on $\mathcal{L}(E)$: its
    93	  proof uses completeness and operator multiplication of norm one, exactly as on
    94	  $\mathcal{L}(F)$. For fixed $s,t$, each left Young sum
    95	  \[
    96	    \sum_j\big(X(t_{j+1})-X(t_j)\big)U_X(t_j,s)
    97	  \]
    98	  is compact. The sums converge in operator norm to $U_X(t,s)-I$, so closedness
    99	  of the compact ideal gives the first assertion
   100	  in~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}. Bounded composition then shows
   101	  that the physical endpoint differs from $S_E(t-s)$ by a compact operator.
   102	
   103	  We prove the required compact-perturbation bound for this whole-space phase.
   104	  Translations $\tau_y$ on both entries are isometries on $E$ and commute with
   105	  $S_E(h)$. For fixed $z,w \in E$, their translated pairing is the Fourier
   106	  transform of an $L^1$ function: the two weighted Fourier products are
   107	  integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz in the Bessel norms. Approximation of that
   108	  function in $L^1$ by compact smooth functions, followed by integration by
   109	  parts for the approximants, proves $\langle\tau_yz,w\rangle_E \to 0$ as $|y|
   110	  \to \infty$. Thus, $\tau_yz$ tends weakly to zero. For compact $K$,
   111	  $\|K\tau_yz\| \to 0$: otherwise compactness supplies a norm-convergent
   112	  subsequence with nonzero norm, while bounded linear testing makes its limit
   113	  zero. For unit $z$ it follows that
   114	  \[
   115	    \|S_E(h)+K\|
   116	    \ge\liminf_{|y|\to\infty}\|(S_E(h)+K)\tau_yz\|
   117	    \ge\|S_E(h)z\|.
   118	  \]
   119	  Taking the supremum over $z$ gives $\|S_E(h)+K\| \ge \|S_E(h)\|$. The
   120	  isometric velocity reversal $\mathcal{R}(u,v) = (u,-v)$ satisfies $S_E(-h) =
   121	  \mathcal{R} S_E(h)\mathcal{R}$ by the full free Fourier matrix. The group law
   122	  yields $1 \le \|S_E(-h)\|\|S_E(h)\| = \|S_E(h)\|^2$. This
   123	  proves~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}.
   124	
   125	  Finally, $P_j-S_E(\ell_j)$ is compact. Telescoping the finite ordered product
   126	  against its free product gives a finite sum of bounded--compact--bounded
   127	  products, hence a compact difference. Only the free factors are combined by
   128	  the group law; no noisy factors are commuted. The same translation argument

   130	  = I$. All assertions are at fixed finite horizons and products; no uniform
   131	  compact approximation in a radius, horizon or number of factors is asserted.
   132	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:symplectic-free}.
   133	\end{proof}
    22	\begin{lemma}[Inclusion into the covariance space and the smooth mean]
    23	  \label{L:positive-raw-embedding}
    24	  For any real Hilbert space $G$ there is a bounded map $J_G:L^2(I;G) \to
    25	  H_t\otimes G$ with
    26	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-bochner-inclusion}

    32	  $H_I$, with
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-raw-mean}

   331	\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic original second-moment constant]
   332	  \label{T:intrinsic-second-moment}
   333	  For every original admissible model with data $(1,0)$ and fixed $x$,
   334	  \begin{equation}\label{E:intrinsic-second-moment-limit}
   335	    \lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-(4-\alpha-a)/(3-\alpha)}
   336	    \log\E|u_\Gamma(T,x)|^2
   337	    =C_2(\Gamma,a)=S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}
   338	    =2^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}.
   339	  \end{equation}
   340	  Its complete variational formula over nonnegative controls is
   341	  \begin{align}
   342	    C_2(\Gamma,a)
   343	    &=\sup_{\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}}
   344	    \left\{2\int_I
   345	    \sqrt{\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   346	    \left(\int h_{\Psi,s}f^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right)}
   347	    \ud s-\frac{v_\Psi}{2}\right\},
   348	    \label{E:intrinsic-positive-formula}\\
   349	    h_{\Psi,s}(x)
   350	    &=\int_I|s-t|^{-a}(\Gamma*\Psi_t)(x)\ud t,\qquad
   351	    v_\Psi=\int_{I\times\R^d}\Psi(s,x)h_{\Psi,s}(x)\ud x\ud s.
   352	    \notag
   353	  \end{align}

   355	  $C_c^\infty(I\times\R^d)$ tests, including nonseparable ones. The covariance

   357	  action is $v_\Psi/2$. For nonzero covariance $0 < C_2 < \infty$. For $\Gamma =

   102	`g_n^{T,x}` (`E:terminal-chain-measure`, main TeX lines 3585-3598), written by
   103	recursion on the last vertex: `chainWeight d 0 T () = 1` and
   104	`chainWeight d (n+1) T s = 1_{0 < s_{n+1} < T} G_{T - s_{n+1}}(ℝ^d) ·
   105	chainWeight d n s_{n+1} (s_1, …, s_n)`, i.e. `1_{[0,T]^n_<}(s) ∏_j G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(ℝ^d)`
   106	with `s_{n+1} = T` and the open ordered simplex `0 < s_1 < ⋯ < s_n < T`
   107	(boundary null).  The spatial pushforward under `y_j = x - Σ_{l ≥ j} w_l`
   108	preserves mass, so `∫ chainWeight d n T = g_n^{T,x}(total)` for every `x`
   109	(Tonelli); the measure `g_n^{T,x}` itself is not constructed in Lean. -/
   110	def chainWeight (d : ℕ) : (n : ℕ) → ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ≥0∞
   111	  | 0, _, _ => 1
   112	  | n + 1, T, s =>
   113	    (if 0 < s (Fin.last n) ∧ s (Fin.last n) < T then waveGreen d (T - s (Fin.last n)) univ else 0) *
   114	      chainWeight d n (s (Fin.last n)) (Fin.init s)

   117	def chainWeightReal : (n : ℕ) → ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ≥0∞
   118	  | 0, _, _ => 1
   119	  | n + 1, T, s =>
   120	    (if 0 < s (Fin.last n) ∧ s (Fin.last n) < T then ENNReal.ofReal (T - s (Fin.last n)) else 0) *
   121	      chainWeightReal n (s (Fin.last n)) (Fin.init s)

   125	    ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ) (s : Fin n → ℝ), chainWeight d n T s = chainWeightReal n T s := by
   126	  intro n
   127	  induction n with
   128	  | zero => intro T s; rfl
   129	  | succ n ih =>
   130	    intro T s
   131	    simp only [chainWeight, chainWeightReal, ih]

   488	
   489	section NormOne
   490	
   491	variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   492	
   493	/-- If `B A = I`, `B = R A R` and `R` is an isometry, then `1 ≤ ‖A‖` (TeX lines
   494	120-122).  `Nontrivial E` is needed: on the zero space every operator has norm zero. -/
   495	theorem one_le_norm_of_reversal [Nontrivial E] (A B R : E →L[ℝ] E) (hBA : B * A = 1)
   496	    (hR : ∀ z, ‖R z‖ = ‖z‖) (hB : B = R * A * R) : 1 ≤ ‖A‖ := by
   497	  have hRn : ‖R‖ ≤ 1 :=
   498	    ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ zero_le_one fun z => by rw [hR, one_mul]
   499	  have hBn : ‖B‖ ≤ ‖A‖ := by
   500	    rw [hB]
   501	    calc ‖R * A * R‖ ≤ ‖R * A‖ * ‖R‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
   502	      _ ≤ (‖R‖ * ‖A‖) * ‖R‖ := by gcongr; exact norm_mul_le _ _
   503	      _ ≤ (1 * ‖A‖) * 1 := by gcongr
   504	      _ = ‖A‖ := by ring
   505	  have h1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ‖B‖ * ‖A‖ := by
   506	    calc (1 : ℝ) = ‖(1 : E →L[ℝ] E)‖ := norm_one.symm
   507	      _ = ‖B * A‖ := by rw [hBA]
   508	      _ ≤ ‖B‖ * ‖A‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
   509	  have hA0 : 0 ≤ ‖A‖ := norm_nonneg _
   510	  nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hBn hA0]
   511	
   512	end NormOne

   515	
   516	/-- Supplied input (D8; TeX lines 103-122): the free wave group `S_E` on
   517	`E = H^{1/2} × H^{-1/2}`, the velocity reversal `𝓡(u,v) = (u,-v)` and the spatial
   518	translations `τ_y`, `y ∈ ℝ^d`, with the properties the proof of `L:symplectic-free`
   519	states for them: the group law, `S_E(-h) = 𝓡 S_E(h) 𝓡` with `𝓡` isometric,
   520	translations isometric and commuting with `S_E(h)`, and `⟨τ_y z, w⟩_E → 0` as
   521	`|y| → ∞` (cocompact filter on `ℝ^d`). -/
   522	structure FreeWaveData (d : ℕ) (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] where
   523	  /-- The free group `S_E(t)`. -/
   524	  S : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E
   525	  S_zero : S 0 = 1
   526	  S_add : ∀ s t, S (s + t) = S s * S t
   527	  /-- The velocity reversal. -/
   528	  R : E →L[ℝ] E
   529	  R_norm : ∀ z, ‖R z‖ = ‖z‖
   530	  S_neg : ∀ h, S (-h) = R * S h * R
   531	  /-- The translations `τ_y`. -/
   532	  τ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → E →L[ℝ] E
   533	  τ_norm : ∀ y z, ‖τ y z‖ = ‖z‖
   534	  τ_comm : ∀ y h, S h * τ y = τ y * S h
   535	  τ_weak : ∀ z w, Tendsto (fun y => inner ℝ (τ y z) w) (cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) (𝓝 0)
   536	
   537	/-- Supplied input (D7; `P:constant-young-linear` on `𝓛(E)`, TeX lines 91-98): the left
   538	Young sums of `X` over partitions of `[s,t]` converge in operator norm to
   539	`U(t,s) - I` along some nontrivial filter of partitions.  A partition is a pair
   540	`(n, p)` with points `p 0, …, p n`; only the points `p j`, `j ≤ n`, enter, and they lie
   541	in `[s,t]` eventually.  The TeX's convergence as the mesh tends to zero implies this
   542	statement (the mesh filter is nontrivial). -/
   543	def LeftYoungSumsConverge {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   544	    (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s t : ℝ) : Prop :=
   545	  ∃ l : Filter (ℕ × (ℕ → ℝ)), l.NeBot ∧
   546	    (∀ᶠ π in l, ∀ j ≤ π.1, π.2 j ∈ Set.Icc s t) ∧
   547	    Tendsto (fun π => youngSum X U s π.2 π.1) l (𝓝 (U t s - 1))
   548

   554	theorem FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
   555	    (cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))).NeBot := by
   556	  have : Nonempty (Fin d) := ⟨⟨0, hd⟩⟩
   557	  infer_instance

   562	    1 ≤ ‖F.S h‖ :=
   563	  one_le_norm_of_reversal (F.S h) (F.S (-h)) F.R

   569	  have := FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot hd

  6279	Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  6280	at `a284420`; statement lines 3703-3727 with the display
  6281	`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3718-3724; proof lines 3729-3748), with every
  6282	conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
  6283	3600-3645), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
  6284	facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3730-3731): absolute `L^2` convergence of
  6285	every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
  6286	states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
  6287	`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
  6288	complex `r`, lines 3643-3644) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
  6289	formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
  6290	and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3638-3641). Nothing else about the Gaussian
  6291	field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
  6292	statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
  6293	two facts. For the chain integrals `Y_n` of a centered Gaussian field with
  6294	nonnegative covariance, `TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (wave L8)
  6295	proves `TerminalWickInput` from that lemma's own inputs, and
  6296	`L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` composes the two; the
  6297	identification of the regularized family `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with such terms is
  6298	not formalized. The
  6299	fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
  6300	`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
  6301	`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
  6302	integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
  6303	product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
  6304	`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
  6305	`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
  6306	real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
  6307	`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
  6308	`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
  6309	`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
  6310	the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
  6311	such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
  6312	convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
  6313	in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
  6314	`E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
  6315	absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
  6316	convergence", lines 3735-3736). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
  6317	last sentence (lines 3725-3726): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
  6318	`eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
  6319	(`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
  6320	used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
  6321	`uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
  6322	space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
  6323	hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
  6324	bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
  6325	dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
  6326	are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
  6327	`u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
  6328	(`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
  6329	`B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
  6330	(lines 3738-3745), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
  6331	the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by
  6332	hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every
  6333	`tsum` is a genuine sum; `B >= 0` follows from the moment bound, so
  6334	`Real.sqrt B` is the true square root; `r > 1` makes `(r^n)^(-1)` and
  6335	`1 - r^(-1)` positive. Not formalized: the regularized family itself (the terms
  6336	`Y_n^{eps,delta}` as terms of `L:terminal-wick`) and the application of the
  6337	lemma to the regularized solution in later proofs; `L:terminal-wick` is in
  6338	`TerminalWick`, with its own inputs.
